question: Can uncertainty from reconstructing survival individual-patient data support a distinct, useful study-decision calibration paper beyond established reconstruction accuracy and uncertainty methods?
priority: Existing rank5 after four verified paper-prospect deprioritizations; broad methods utility, weak EMC specificity, novelty unproven. Do not infer clinical effects from sparse EMC reconstruction.
scope: First specify a concrete study decision, estimand and ground-truth validation route. Inspect existing evidence and targeted primary reconstruction/uncertainty benchmarks, including IPDfromKM and original reconstruction methods. If a distinct remediable gap exists, run a small explicitly synthetic or public-known-IPD feasibility experiment using matched reconstruction baselines; retain negative results and reproducible inputs/scripts. Avoid inventing clinical thresholds, generic accuracy simulation, or unnecessary full-corpus work.
success: A concrete novel decision-level question with actual primary prior-art distinction and credible falsifiable validation, ideally one reproduced informative pilot result. This is a development gate, not publication adequacy.
failure: Existing methods answer the question, no adequate ground truth or identifiable estimand, arbitrary thresholds, or only routine digitization-error simulations/sparse disease-effect inference.
stop: One fresh worker with its own bounded goal,medium,1800seconds,no nested tasks/agents/runners. Return go/no-go or one exact remediable uncertainty. No manuscript/preregistration/clinical registry edits, publication or outreach, paid API/GPU spending. Overall mission has no daily pacing cap.
